metadata.goal: Identify the major changes in movement behavior during the trip and detect abnormal movement segments.
metadata.dataset_description: A point-level WorldTrace trip includes location, speed, yaw change, movement phase, cumulative distance, direct displacement, and excess distance.

insight_list.insight: The strongest speed reductions consistently occur around the sharpest bends in the route, while movement remains relatively stable along straight road sections.

plot.title: Speed Reductions and Route Bends
plot.description: Yaw-change and speed evidence is shown both as a relationship and along the trip sequence.

insight_list.question: Where do the largest speed reductions occur relative to route curvature?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare speed distributions at high-yaw and low-yaw points and check their positions in the sequence.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
d=df.copy(); d['bend']=pd.cut(d.yaw_change_deg,[-1,10,35,181],labels=['straight','moderate','sharp']); print(d.groupby('bend').speed_kmh.mean()); plt.scatter(d.yaw_change_deg,d.speed_kmh,c=pd.Categorical(d.bend).codes); plt.show()

insight_list.insight: The trip remains direct for most of the journey but becomes slow and locally circuitous near the destination, where repeated turns account for most of the excess travel distance.

plot.title: Destination Circuit, Speed, and Excess Distance
plot.description: The route map is paired with the same speed sequence used for the mid-trip-disruption view and with per-step excess-distance additions, separating the middle slowdown from destination-area detours.

insight_list.question: Which part of the journey contributes most of the repeated turns and excess travel distance?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Relate destination-area geometry to the speed phase and to per-step additions of excess distance.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
d=df.copy(); d['excess_added_km']=d.excess_distance_km.diff().fillna(0); fig,ax=plt.subplots(2,2); ax[0,0].plot(d.x_km,d.y_km); ax[0,1].plot(d.point_index,d.speed_kmh); ax[1,1].bar(d.point_index,d.excess_added_km); plt.show(); print(d.groupby('movement_phase').yaw_change_deg.mean())

insight_list.insight: A prolonged low-speed segment appears in the middle of the trip despite relatively smooth movement before and after it, making this section the primary disruption to an otherwise stable journey.

plot.title: Mid-Trip Low-Speed Disruption
plot.description: A highlighted continuous interval distinguishes the prolonged mid-trip disruption from brief bend-related reductions.

insight_list.question: Is there a prolonged low-speed interval away from the destination, and how does movement before and after it compare?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare the highlighted interval with adjacent stable-corridor speeds and with the later destination phase.
insight_list.code:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
d=df.copy(); d['mid_disruption']=d.point_index.between(42,58); print(d.groupby('mid_disruption').speed_kmh.mean()); plt.plot(d.point_index,d.speed_kmh); plt.axvspan(42,58,color='orange',alpha=.25); plt.show()

insights: The strongest speed reductions consistently occur around the sharpest bends in the route, while movement remains relatively stable along straight road sections.
The trip remains direct for most of the journey but becomes slow and locally circuitous near the destination, where repeated turns account for most of the excess travel distance.
A prolonged low-speed segment appears in the middle of the trip despite relatively smooth movement before and after it, making this section the primary disruption to an otherwise stable journey.
summary: The journey is mostly stable and direct, but three movement changes stand out: brief speed reductions at sharp bends, a prolonged low-speed disruption in the middle, and a slow, repeatedly turning destination phase where most excess distance accumulates.
